observation_summary: The application throws an 'Operation not supported' exception when attempting to serialize binary data using an InputStream, because the ToXmlGenerator class lacks an implementation for the writeBinary(Base64Variant, InputStream, int) method.
hypothesis: The ToXmlGenerator class is missing a required capability (the writeBinary method for InputStreams) that is expected by the Jackson serialization framework, causing it to fall back to an unsupported operation.
prediction: Implementing the writeBinary method in ToXmlGenerator, along with helper methods to read the InputStream into a buffer or stream it as binary, will resolve the exception.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of the missing writeBinary method and supporting logic (writeStreamAsBinary, toFullBuffer), which directly addresses the 'Operation not supported' error by providing the missing functionality.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of a missing capability. The class ToXmlGenerator failed to implement a method required by the Jackson API contract for binary data serialization. This is not a local algorithmic error or a simple value assignment, but the absence of a necessary design-level capability that the framework expects the generator to provide.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding a method, the root cause is the complete absence of a required capability in the class design, not an error in an existing algorithm.
